title: Swap the glemy git dependency for the real Hex release, 0.1.0
context: This repo's gleam.toml depended on glemy via a git dependency pinned to commit f5aa0437 since the split (see glemy's own docs/decisions.jsonl for that decision). glemy published a real 0.1.0 release to Hex shortly after. glemy's own ARCHITECTURE.md always framed the git dependency as a transitional bridge until a real Hex release existed.

options_considered.option: Keep the git dependency, since it already works and there's no forcing function to change it
options_considered.reason: A real Hex release now exists, and this repo's own ARCHITECTURE.md already documented the git dependency as transitional. Delaying the swap only means re-deriving 'why haven't we done this yet' later, for no benefit -- the change is small, low-risk, and immediately verifiable.

decision: Changed gleam.toml's `glemy = { git = "...", ref = "f5aa0437..." }` to `glemy = ">= 0.1.0 and < 0.2.0"`. Re-resolved dependencies (`gleam deps download` correctly reported 'Added glemy v0.1.0 / Removed glemy'), updated the checked-in `manifest.toml` lock, updated ARCHITECTURE.md/CLAUDE.md's own description of the dependency mechanism, and updated the warnings baseline (122 -> 85 warnings).
verification: gleam build/gleam test both targets pass in full (118 Erlang / 125 JavaScript, unchanged), deno task check-warnings passes against the updated baseline, and all three real browser-checks (Tiers/Breakout/Platformer) pass against a live dev server. A fresh GitHub Actions CI run (no local build cache) also passed green, confirming the Hex resolution works from a cold checkout, not just locally.
consequences: Discovered and fixed a real, previously-unnoticed side effect while investigating: the git-dependency commit (f5aa0437) actually predated game removal from glemy's own repo (that removal was a later commit), so this repo had been silently pulling in a stray, unused copy of the game files via the dependency itself the whole time -- harmless (no module-path collisions, since this repo's own game code lives under glemy_games/, not glemy/), but genuinely dead weight, now gone. All 37 warnings that dropped from the baseline traced directly to that stray copy, confirmed individually before updating rather than assumed. Future glemy releases now flow in via ordinary `gleam deps download` within the `>= 0.1.0 and < 0.2.0` range; widening that range (a new minor/major) is its own deliberate decision, not automatic.
